title: 3 days Upper 2 days Lower program review (for an advanced calisthenics guy part.
summary: Part one of a review of Lawrence's upper/lower program. Lawrence is a former calisthenics athlete with a strong upper body and lagging legs who wants a classic physique. NH approves most compounds, criticizes feel-based high-rep arm work and banded hamstring curls, and asks for daily upper-back work, more volume on upper days, plus forearm, calf and neck guidance.
claims: Street workout athletes accumulate a huge tonnage debt in the legs, because skipped squat sessions represent far more weight than skipped bicep sessions
Being very good at calisthenics requires smaller legs; as legs grow they load calisthenics movements, so expect to sacrifice some calisthenics strength for months to a year
Someone who can do 30 clean pull-ups should weight all vertical pulls in a bodybuilding context
Classic physiques like Lee Labrada or Frank Zane had medium legs, not tree trunks, so upper body focus can remain
Some lifters need long sessions (diesel engines that warm up slowly), others are quick-start fuel that fades fast; he can train four hours without noticing time
Strict form with 3-second negatives and full ROM is good for injury prevention, but don't lock yourself into only training that way
Intensity, frequency and volume always exist; you can lean toward whichever suits you mentally or gives results, as long as all three are applied
Consistency matters most: a program you'll follow for 10 years beats one that burns you out in three months
Don't judge whether you're past the novice phase from strength numbers
Push progression on everything; at advanced stages any carryover gains must be secured, so don't go purely by feel
Barbell rows fit well on upper days because you aren't fatigued from squats or deadlifts; 4x8-10 is a good range
Bench 4x6-8 is a good range; rows and bench can be supersetted without strength loss
With a two-rep window, an occasional matched rep count across sets is OK at higher reps but suggests poor intensity control at low reps like 5
Lateral raises supersetted with face pulls pre-fatigue the traps so rear delts work on face pulls; his own traps take over face pulls
He's a big fan of barbell overhead press after bench, strength focused, 3x6-8
Superset OHP with bodyweight AMRAP pull-ups to maintain pull-up fitness; rows already cover upper back intensity
Going by feel for arms at 12-20 reps is too much volume; naturals build arms with progressive overload
Train biceps at 6-10 reps; he personally uses 3-7 reps for advanced lifters; keep one pump movement as the exception
Compounds are attractive because they drive tonnage best, not because they're mandatory
Upper body days should be longer than lower body days; that's where lagging parts get supersetted in
Rotating three lunge variations is fine because they're far enough from the squat; you want stimulus there, not carryover
Squats and deadlifts are self-sufficient and can grow from themselves; bench needs more variation and flies won't carry over to it
He's not a fan of rotating exercises every 8-12 weeks because it looks like block training, but it's fine for lunges
Most people who say they do RDLs actually do stiff-legged deadlifts; 4x8-10 is excellent for that lift
Drop awkward banded hamstring curls since stiff-legged deadlifts already give the stretch; if you like them, do them on rest days to boost recovery
Back hyperextensions followed by leg raises is the golden combo for people with back pain, decompressing the spine and helping hip health
Forearms: start wrist flexion once a week, then twice, then add a variation
Calves are the dumbest body part: just progressively overload calf raises, lots of volume, 3x/week; his calves grew an inch this year that way
With strong upper back recovery, train upper back every day via rows, shrugs or pull-ups
Superset stiff-legged deadlifts with shrugs using the same bar: finish the set, stand, squeeze glutes and shrug
Weighted pull-ups on two days are fine for an advanced lifter; change the grip to avoid injury
exercises: best on upper day when fresh
pre-fatigue traps so rear delts work
superset after stiff-legged deadlift with same bar
calisthenics athlete too strong for bodyweight
